settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Everything is configured here: no file to edit, nothing to restart. Values live in the hub's database and travel with your backups.
settings.influx_url_hint: The address the hub uses to reach Influx from inside the container. This is not the one probes receive.
settings.heartbeat_hint: The “online” status covers three intervals: at 60 s, a probe turns to “no news” after three minutes of silence. Probes pick up the new interval on their next heartbeat.
settings.retention_hint: Applied to the InfluxDB bucket. Extending it has no effect on existing measurements; shortening it deletes some. 0 = keep forever.
settings.shrink_cutoff: Every measurement older than {date} will be permanently deleted by InfluxDB, for every probe of every site.
settings.shrink_irreversible: The deletion is performed by the time-series database: it cannot be undone, and the hub keeps no copy.
settings.shrink_ack: I understand that measurements older than {date} will be deleted.
settings.invalid_url: Enter a full URL, for example https://127.0.0.1:8086.
settings.invalid_retention: Retention is a whole number of days, 0 or more.
settings.invalid_heartbeat: The interval must be at least 10 seconds.
settings.influx_lead: This is the address a probe receives at enrolment to write its measurements to. The hub reaches Influx locally — a probe on the network does not.
settings.why_body: A container does not know which port it was published on. With -p 9086:8086 the process only ever sees 8086; nobody tells it about 9086. No detection can guess the right value, hence this field.
settings.order_1: The value set here, if it is filled in.
settings.order_3: Otherwise the address the probe used to reach the hub, with the Influx port.
settings.field_hint: Leave empty to let the hub work it out: standard ports and no reverse proxy work with nothing set. Fill it in if the Influx port is remapped, or if probes reach it through another hostname.
settings.saved: URL saved. Probes enrolled from now on will get it; probes already in place keep theirs.
settings.unreachable_title: Influx does not answer at this address
settings.unreachable_body: A probe enrolled with this URL would enrol without any error, show up online in the fleet, and never write anything. Enter above the address reachable from the probes' network, published port included: if the container publishes Influx as -p 9086:8086, write 9086 here, not 8086.
settings.test_failed: The test could not be run.
settings.influx_state_lead: There is nothing for you to administer in InfluxDB: the organisation and the bucket are created on first start. This block is here so you know where your measurements live and whether all is well.
settings.tokens_lead: A read-only token on the bucket: it lets you point Grafana or another tool at your measurements, without being able to write or delete any.
settings.tokens_once_title: Copy it now: it will never be shown again
settings.tokens_once_body: The hub keeps only its identifier, so it can revoke it. The value below exists nowhere else: close this window without copying it and you will have to generate another.
settings.tokens_revoke_body: Whatever uses it loses access to the measurements as soon as it is revoked. Nothing is deleted: the measurements stay, only this token stops working.
settings.tls_body: Influx is served over HTTPS with a certificate generated on first start. Probes pin its fingerprint, handed over at enrolment: nothing to install on the monitored machine.

setup.title: First run
setup.lead: No account exists on this hub yet. Create the administrator: this is the account that sees the fleet and that probes authenticate against to enrol.
setup.token_where: The hub generated this token at startup and wrote it to its logs. On the machine hosting the container:
setup.token_alt: It is also written into the volume, readable by root only:
setup.token_once: The token works once: as soon as the account exists, it is worthless.
setup.token_hint_name: If you renamed the container, replace lanprobe-web with its name.
setup.password_hint: 12 characters minimum. This account opens the measurements of the whole fleet.
setup.err_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
setup.err_token: Paste the setup token printed in the container logs.

auth.title: Sign in
auth.expired: Your session expired. Sign in again.
auth.unreachable: The hub did not answer. Check that the container is running.
auth.cookie_blocked: Signed in, but your browser refused the session cookie. Open a private window, or delete this site's cookies — a cookie left by an earlier HTTPS visit to the same address blocks the new one.

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.count: {n, plural, =0 {no probes} one {# probe} other {# probes}}
fleet.site_count: {n, plural, =0 {no sites} one {# site} other {# sites}}
fleet.empty_sites_body: The hub is up and waiting for its first probe. Enrolment always starts from the probe: the token has to land on the machine that measures, not in this browser. The site is created along the way, from the name you type on the probe.
fleet.empty_site_title: This site has no probe yet
fleet.empty_site_body: The site “{name}” exists, but no probe has enrolled into it. Enrol one from the machine you want to watch, using this site name.
fleet.empty_site_cta: Add a probe to this site
fleet.error_title: The fleet could not be loaded
fleet.no_match_body: This filter returns nothing. The fleet itself holds {n, plural, one {# probe} other {# probes}}.

status.stale_help: Silent for more than three intervals, less than 24 h.

buffer.label: Buffer
buffer.pending: {n, plural, one {# point waiting to be written} other {# points waiting to be written}}
buffer.warn_title: {n, plural, one {# probe is piling up} other {# probes are piling up}} measurements without writing them
buffer.warn_body: A probe's buffer only fills when writing to InfluxDB fails. While it grows, those probes' charts have a hole — a hole that closes on replay, or becomes permanent if the buffer overflows.

site.create_hint: A site groups the probes of one customer. It is also created on its own when a probe enrols mentioning a site the hub does not know.
site.rename_warning_title: Measurements already written keep the old name
site.rename_warning_body: Points recorded before this rename still carry the “{name}” label in Grafana. They stay attached to this site — the join is on the identifier, not the name — only the readable label diverges, until the probes pick up the new name on their next heartbeat.
site.conflict: A site named “{name}” already exists. Case does not count: “Durand” and “durand” are the same site.
site.empty_name: The site name cannot be empty.
site.populated_note: This site holds {n, plural, one {# probe} other {# probes}}. A populated site cannot be retired: move its probes to another site, or revoke them, before retiring the site.
site.probe_count: {n, plural, =0 {no probes} one {# probe} other {# probes}}

probe.rename_hint: The name is a label: changing it does not touch the measurement history.
probe.rename_conflict: A probe named “{name}” already exists in site “{site}”. Two sites may each have their own “{name}”, but not the same site twice.
probe.move_hint: History follows the probe: its charts stay complete after the move, because they are joined on its identifier rather than its site.
probe.move_conflict: Site “{site}” already holds a probe named “{name}”. Rename it before moving.
probe.not_found_body: This probe is no longer in the fleet. It may have been removed from another tab.
probe.keys_intro: Every probe has its own key: revoking one affects no other. Neither of these actions deletes any measurement.
probe.rotate_hint: Routine hygiene. The hub prepares a new key and hands it to the probe on its next heartbeat; the old one is destroyed only once the probe has confirmed. A powered-off probe catches up on the rotation when it wakes, losing nothing.
probe.rotate_done: New key prepared. It will be handed over on the next heartbeat.
probe.pending_title: New key waiting to be handed over
probe.pending_body: It goes out on the next heartbeat. The old key stays valid until the probe confirms it took the new one — that is what stops a powered-off probe from being cut off at the wrong moment.
probe.revoke_now_hint: Keep this for a key that leaked: stolen machine, exposed token.
probe.revoke_now_body: The old key is destroyed right away. The probe will not be able to write measurements until its next contact with the hub, where it receives the new one — that is the intended behaviour when a key leaks: cut first, restore afterwards.
probe.revoke_now_keeps: No measurement is deleted here either.
probe.revoke_now_done: Key revoked. The probe will get a new one on its next contact.
probe.reenroll_hint: For a compromised machine, when someone is on site but is not technical: you read out an address and an eight-character code, they have no account to create and nothing to understand.
probe.reenroll_keeps: The probe comes back with the same identifier, so with all of its history.
probe.reenroll_keeps_body: Its charts are not cut in two at the date of the incident — which is exactly when you want to compare before and after. Re-enrolment replaces both the probe token and its write key, so the compromised machine's credentials are worth nothing.
probe.which_leak: The key leaked but the machine is sound: “Revoke immediately” is enough. The probe repairs itself on its next heartbeat, nobody needs to go on site.
probe.which_host: The machine itself is compromised: this needs a re-enrolment, so someone in front of the probe's screen.

charts.latency_sub: ICMP round-trip time measured by this probe, in milliseconds.
charts.internet_sub: State as seen from the probe. The band gets taller as severity rises.
charts.speed_sub: Results of the speed tests run by this probe.
charts.empty_hint: Widen the window, or check that the matching task is enabled on the probe.
charts.error_shape: The hub answered in a shape this interface cannot read (keys: {keys}).

revoke.title: Remove “{name}” from the fleet?
revoke.body: The probe's token is revoked: it can no longer send heartbeats or write measurements. Nothing is erased from the time-series database — this probe's history stays readable.
revoke.rejoin: To put it back in service you will have to enrol it again; it will get a new token.
revoke.done: “{name}” was removed from the fleet. Its measurements are kept.

code.title: Enrolment code
code.lead: A short code, valid for 15 minutes, usable once. It is all you type into the probe's app, together with the hub address — no username, no password on the monitored machine.
code.expired_body: A code lasts 15 minutes and works once. Generate a new one: nothing is lost, the probe has not been enrolled yet.
code.no_site: Create a site first: an enrolment code is always tied to a site.
code.used_hint: As soon as the probe uses it, the code is worthless. No need to delete it or keep it.
code.site_created: The site will be created at enrolment if it does not exist yet.
code.dictate_enroll: Read out: “Open LanProbe, go to Settings, then Server connection. Type in this address, then this code.”
code.dictate_reenroll: Read out: “Open LanProbe, go to Settings, then Server connection. Type in this address, then this code.” Nothing else to do, and no account to create.

enroll.title: Enrol a probe
enroll.lead: Two values to type into the probe's app: this hub's address and a code. That is all.
enroll.manual_body: Useful for scripted enrolment. The probe then sends this account's username and password, plus the site name and the probe name. Avoid it on a machine you do not control: a compromised host should not hand over the interface credentials.
enroll.step1_title: Open LanProbe on the machine to monitor
enroll.step1_body: Desktop app or headless service. The hub needs a version that knows how to enrol; older builds do not have the screen.
enroll.step3_body: The ones for this account. They are used once, at enrolment, and are never written to the probe's disk.
enroll.step4_body: The probe lists the existing sites; pick yours. A name that is not in the list creates a new site, and the app says so — that is what stops a typo from building a ghost fleet.
enroll.step4_site: For this page, the site is “{site}”.
enroll.step5_body: “Paris”, “Warehouse” — a name you will recognise in a list of thirty. It stays editable later without losing the charts.
enroll.step6_title: It shows up in the fleet
enroll.step6_body: On the first heartbeat, so under a minute after enrolment.
enroll.note: A probe name is unique inside a site, not across the hub: two sites may each have their own “Paris”.
enroll.advertise_title: InfluxDB URL handed to the probe
enroll.advertise_body: This is the address the probe will receive to write its measurements to. Check it before enrolling: a wrong URL gives you a probe that enrols without error, shows up online in the fleet, and never writes anything.
